html:
From 26 to 29 November 2008 ten gunmen held parts of Mumbai for sixty hours and killed 166 people. In India the attack is known as 26/11.

The men belonged to Lashkar-e-Taiba, a militant group based in Pakistan. They sailed from Karachi, seized an Indian fishing boat, killed its crew and came ashore in a rubber dinghy after dark. They split into pairs with rifles, grenades and bombs.

Their targets were chosen to be crowded or foreign:

  • the main railway station, where two of them shot 58 people in the hall;
  • a cafe popular with tourists;
  • a Jewish centre, where a rabbi and his wife were among the dead;
  • two luxury hotels, the Taj Mahal Palace and the Oberoi, where they hunted guests floor by floor.

Handlers in Pakistan directed them by phone, watching the live television coverage. Commandos took until the morning of the 29th to clear the Taj.

Nine attackers were killed. The tenth, Ajmal Kasab, was caught alive by a policeman who held on to the barrel of his rifle and died doing it. Kasab was tried and hanged in 2012.

India broke off peace talks with Pakistan. Pakistan admitted that the plot was partly planned on its soil, but its trials of the organisers stalled.
sum: From 26 to 29 November 2008 ten gunmen held parts of Mumbai for sixty hours and killed 166 people. In India the attack is known as 26/11.
